8
The graph shows the variation of velocity with time for a stone that falls from a bridge into a lake
and sinks to the bottom of the lake.
velocity
0
0
time
What can be deduced about the motion of the stone?
A
Terminal velocity was reached in air.
B
The acceleration in air was decreasing with increasing time.
C
The distance travelled in water was greater than the distance travelled in air.
D
The rate of change of velocity in air was constant.

hints: Look at the first section of the velocity-time graph from $t = 0$ to the peak velocity just before the sudden drop into water, and notice how its steepness changes.
Remember that the gradient of a velocity-time graph is acceleration $a = \Delta v / \Delta t$, so a gradient that flattens means acceleration is changing.
Ask whether the air section becomes flat for terminal velocity, stays straight for constant acceleration, or curves with falling gradient because air resistance increases with speed.
walkthrough: Identify the two main phases: the rising curved part in air ending at maximum velocity, then the rapid decrease on hitting the lake followed by a low constant velocity while sinking.
State the graph rule: gradient of a velocity-time graph equals acceleration, and area under the graph equals distance travelled.
Observe the air section: it starts steep and its gradient continuously decreases with time, so it is not a straight line and never becomes horizontal before impact.
Explain the cause: as velocity increases, air resistance increases, so the resultant downward force and hence acceleration $a = F_{net}/m$ decrease with time.

Check the other ideas: no flat top in air rules out terminal velocity in air, a curved graph rules out constant rate of change of velocity, and the much larger velocities in air give larger area than the slow sinking in water.
Therefore the only deduction supported by the decreasing gradient in air is decreasing acceleration. This is option B.

A.explanation: Terminal velocity in air would need a horizontal velocity-time section before the sharp drop at water entry, but the velocity is still increasing up to impact.

B.explanation: The gradient of the velocity-time graph equals acceleration, and the gradient of the curved air-fall section gets smaller with time as air resistance grows.

C.explanation: Distance is the area under the velocity-time graph, and the high-velocity air section encloses a larger area than the low-velocity sinking section in water.

D.explanation: A constant rate of change of velocity would give a straight line with constant gradient, but the air-fall section is clearly curved.
